title: What does the winner pay?
hook: Three bidders, one lamp, a price that rises a dollar at a time. Where does it stop?

knows: people stop bidding once the price passes what the item is worth to them
doesNotKnow: that the winner of a rising-price auction pays about the runner-up's value, not their own

misconception: In a rising-price auction the winner pays close to what the item is worth to them.
objective: The learner can explain that a rising-price auction stops when the second-highest bidder quits, so with values $70, $55 and $40 the winner pays $56, about what a sealed second-price auction charges ($55).

claims.text: With values $70, $55 and $40, a price rising $1 at a time and each bidder quitting once it passes their value, the $40 bidder quits at $41, the $55 bidder quits at $56, and the $70 bidder wins at $56, keeping $14.
claims.source: Lesson rule (bidder in while price <= value). Builder's node script (scratchpad ncm-e01-checks/check.mjs) and Demo.tsx FINAL: raising from $30 by $1, two bidders remain until $56, when only the $70 bidder is left. 70 - 56 = 14. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): node re-run of inAt()/over(): from $30 by $1, 2 bidders in through $55, 1 at $56; Cal out at $41, Ben out at $56; 70 - 56 = 14. Stage 'quit at $value+1'.

claims.text: For one item, any price above $55 and up to $70 leaves exactly one willing buyer, and the rising price stops at the first such price.
claims.source: Count of bidders with value >= price: 2 at $55, 1 for $56..$70, 0 above $70; a $1 rising procedure from below stops at the first price with one bidder left ($56). E&K ch. 10 (market-clearing prices; chapter only, section unconfirmed). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): count of values >= p: 2 at 55, 1 for 56..70, 0 above 70 (node). E&K ch. 10 (matching markets, market-clearing prices) placement matches my knowledge; section not confirmed.

claims.text: A sealed second-price auction with the same values would charge $55, nearly the same as the rising auction.
claims.source: Second-price rule: winner pays the second-highest bid; with truthful bids that is $55. Equivalence of the ascending (English) auction and the sealed second-price auction for private values: W. Vickrey, 'Counterspeculation, auctions, and competitive sealed tenders', Journal of Finance 16(1), 8-37 (1961); E&K ch. 9. Citation from memory; fact-checker confirms. | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): second-highest value 55 vs 56 rising. Vickrey, J. Finance 16(1):8-37 (1961) confirmed bibliographically via search; not opened. claims.text: The stage is a model: each bidder knows their own value and quits the moment the price passes it.
claims.source: Modelling choice stated on the card (private values, no bidding above value, $1 steps). | FC pass 22 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Demo.tsx rules and muted line match.

recall.question: In an open auction where the price keeps rising until one bidder is left, what mostly sets the price the winner pays?
options: The value of the last bidder to quit
The average of all the values
recall.why: The price stops rising as soon as the runner-up quits, so the winner pays just above the runner-up's value; the winner's value only decides who wins.
